consult_notes.note_text: Asked to see a 36-year-old man from Haiti with four months of fever, dry cough, night sweats and weight loss, and a diffuse miliary nodular pattern on imaging. We reviewed the Chart so far. With this presentation and origin in a high-incidence country, disseminated mycobacterial infection is the leading concern; endemic fungal infection is the main alternative. Please keep him in an airborne-isolation room until infection is excluded. No single test is sensitive enough in disseminated disease, so sample widely and do not let one negative result reassure you.
recommendations: Airborne isolation
Three sputum samples for AFB smear, MTB PCR and mycobacterial culture
HIV test, and hepatitis B and C serology as a baseline
If sputum is negative, bronchoscopy with lavage for AFB, PCR and culture, and transbronchial biopsy
Urine and blood mycobacterial cultures; fungal antigens (cryptococcal, histoplasma)
An interferon-gamma release assay adds little: a negative result does not exclude disease
If suspicion stays high after sampling, start empirical four-drug antimycobacterial treatment

consult_notes.note_text: Reviewed again with the negative sputum and lavage results, the negative sequencing and the transbronchial biopsy showing non-necrotising granulomas. None of this excludes disseminated mycobacterial infection: smears, PCR, interferon-gamma release assays and cell-free DNA are all insensitive in miliary disease, and granulomas without necrosis occur in it. The picture has not changed. We would not attribute this to sarcoidosis while infection remains this likely, and we advise against steroids without antimycobacterial cover.
recommendations: Start empirical four-drug antimycobacterial treatment now
If steroids are considered, give them only with antimycobacterial treatment already started
Send marrow, liver or urine samples for AFB stain, PCR and culture if another site is sampled
Repeat testing, including sequencing, if he deteriorates

consult_notes.note_text: The MTB complex results from the repeat sequencing and the second lavage confirm the infection we were concerned about. Start rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol today, dosed for his liver and kidney function, with daily liver tests. Continue airborne isolation. With the trigger now being treated, further etoposide should be withheld; dexamethasone may continue at the haematology team's discretion. Please notify public health so his household can be screened.
recommendations: Start four-drug treatment today
Withhold further etoposide
Airborne isolation
Notify public health; screen household contacts
Check drug susceptibility on the culture isolate

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about diffuse miliary nodules with four months of fever and cough. We reviewed the Chart so far. The random distribution of the nodules, with no hilar lymph node enlargement, points to haematogenous spread of an infection rather than to sarcoidosis, which usually follows the lymphatics and comes with hilar nodes. Saturation is mildly reduced at rest.
recommendations: Induced or early-morning sputum for AFB, PCR and culture first
We are happy to do bronchoscopy with lavage and transbronchial biopsy if sputum is negative
Airborne precautions for the procedure

consult_notes.note_text: The transbronchial biopsy shows non-necrotising granulomas with negative stains. This does not separate infection from sarcoidosis: granulomas without necrosis occur in disseminated mycobacterial infection, and sarcoidosis remains a diagnosis of exclusion. Given the random nodules, the fever and the absence of hilar nodes, we would not call this sarcoidosis.
recommendations: Ask the laboratory to hold tissue for mycobacterial culture and PCR
Treat infection first if steroids are being considered

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about a mild normocytic anaemia with lymphopenia and a very high ferritin in a febrile man with splenomegaly. We reviewed the Chart so far. The pattern fits anaemia of chronic inflammation, and a ferritin at this level is an acute-phase response to his illness. There is nothing to suggest a primary blood disorder at present.
recommendations: Blood film
Repeat counts and ferritin
Marrow examination if the counts fall further, with samples sent for mycobacterial culture as well as morphology

consult_notes.note_text: Reviewed with the falling counts, rising ferritin and transaminases, the soluble IL-2 receptor and CXCL9 results and the marrow. Together with the fever and splenomegaly these meet the criteria for a secondary haemophagocytic process. The trigger matters more than the marrow findings: in a man with marrow and lung granulomas, the likeliest trigger is the underlying granulomatous infection, and immunosuppression alone will not control it.
recommendations: Treat the trigger; antimycobacterial treatment should be in place before or with any etoposide or further steroid
Dexamethasone may be used alongside treatment of the trigger
Send marrow for AFB stain, PCR and culture if not already done
Transfuse red cells and platelets to usual thresholds; monitor fibrinogen

consult_notes.note_text: With the MTB complex results, the haemophagocytic process has a treatable trigger. We agree with withholding further etoposide now that four-drug treatment has started; continue dexamethasone and blood product support.
recommendations: Withhold further etoposide
Continue dexamethasone and transfusion support

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about possible sarcoidosis. We reviewed the Chart so far. Sarcoidosis is a diagnosis of exclusion; with high fever, weight loss, random miliary nodules without hilar nodes and origin in a high-incidence country, infection has to be excluded first, and a raised ACE does not separate the two. There are no eye, skin or joint features of sarcoidosis.
recommendations: Exclude infection before any steroid
Slit-lamp examination
ACE is not diagnostic

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about possible malignancy. We reviewed the Chart so far. There is no lymph node mass, no focal organ lesion and no abnormal cell population in the blood; the pattern does not suggest lymphoma or metastatic cancer.
recommendations: Marrow and flow cytometry if the counts fall
No oncological intervention indicated

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to examine the eyes. Visual acuity 6/6 in each eye. Anterior segments quiet with no uveitis. Dilated fundoscopy: optic discs and vessels normal; no choroidal lesions, haemorrhages or exudates.
recommendations: No ophthalmic treatment needed

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about tachycardia. We reviewed the Chart so far. The sinus tachycardia fits the fever and anaemia. The echocardiogram shows no vegetations, pericardial effusion or dysfunction.
recommendations: No cardiac intervention needed
Treat the fever and anaemia

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to assess for neurological involvement. He is alert with no focal deficit and no meningism; the only headache is with the fevers. There is no clinical evidence of meningitis or of focal brain lesions.
recommendations: Lumbar puncture and MRI only if headache, confusion or focal signs develop, or before steroids if meningeal involvement is suspected

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about abnormal liver tests. We reviewed the Chart so far. A raised ALP and GGT with a modest transaminase rise and splenomegaly suggest an infiltrative process in the liver; granulomatous disease is the likeliest in this context. Viral hepatitis serology is negative.
recommendations: Ultrasound abdomen
Liver biopsy can sample granulomas for histology, AFB stain and culture if other sites are unhelpful
Monitor liver tests closely, especially if liver-toxic treatment starts

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about kidney function. We reviewed the Chart so far. Renal function was normal on admission. If it worsens, the likeliest causes here are reduced perfusion and nephrotoxic medicines rather than primary kidney disease.
recommendations: Avoid nephrotoxic medicines
Dose drugs for kidney function
Renal replacement therapy if needed in shock

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about the sodium and glucose. We reviewed the Chart so far. The mild hyponatraemia fits inappropriate ADH secretion with his lung disease. High-dose steroid will raise glucose and suppress cortisol; a low cortisol on steroid does not mean adrenal failure.
recommendations: Capillary glucose monitoring on steroids
Insulin if glucose stays above 11 mmol/L
Stress-dose hydrocortisone in shock if steroids have been stopped

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to review nutrition. Weight 62 kg, BMI 19.6 kg/m², with about 10 kg lost over four months and a poor appetite. Albumin is low.
recommendations: High-energy, high-protein diet with oral supplements
Weekly weights

final_dx.text: Miliary tuberculosis with repeatedly negative initial microbiological tests, mistaken for sarcoidosis on non-necrotising granulomas, treated with high-dose steroid and complicated by secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis

key_discriminators: Random miliary nodules with four months of fever, cough, night sweats and weight loss
The low sensitivity of every single TB test in miliary disease
No response to high-dose steroid, then worsening
Pancytopenia with rising ferritin and transaminases (secondary haemophagocytosis)
Repeat sequencing and second lavage AFB stain and PCR positive on day 25

must_do.text: Keep tuberculosis high on the list despite negative tests, given the miliary pattern, the symptoms and the origin
Start empirical anti-tuberculosis treatment when suspicion stays high despite negative tests, and before or with any steroid
Send samples from more than one site (sputum and lavage, marrow, urine, blood or liver) for AFB stain, MTB PCR and mycobacterial culture, and repeat testing when the course changes
Recognise secondary haemophagocytosis (cytopenias, ferritin, triglycerides, fibrinogen, soluble IL-2 receptor, marrow) and treat its trigger
Isolate the patient while tuberculosis is possible and involve infectious diseases early
Notify public health and arrange screening of household contacts

must_not_do.text: Diagnose sarcoidosis and start high-dose steroid without anti-tuberculosis cover while miliary tuberculosis has not been reliably excluded
Treat haemophagocytosis with etoposide or escalating immunosuppression without treating the trigger
Take a negative interferon-gamma release assay, smears or sequencing as excluding miliary tuberculosis and commit to sarcoidosis

ground_truth.outcome: Multi-organ failure; died about one week after starting anti-tuberculosis treatment. Autopsy declined, so whether tuberculosis was present from the start or reactivated under immunosuppression is not proven; the authors think it was present from the start, and the case follows them.
red_herrings: Negative sputum AFB smears, MTB PCR and mycobacterial cultures
Negative first cell-free DNA and pathogen sequencing
Non-necrotising (non-caseating) granulomas in the lung and marrow

rubric.text: Miliary (disseminated) tuberculosis with secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis recognised
Miliary or other tuberculosis without recognising the haemophagocytosis, or haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with tuberculosis named as its trigger
Another disseminated granulomatous infection (non-tuberculous mycobacteria, histoplasmosis)
Sarcoidosis, lymphoma or haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis without its trigger
Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: In miliary disease a negative IGRA, smear, PCR, culture or even cell-free DNA sequencing does not exclude tuberculosis; pretest probability should drive empirical treatment.
Non-necrotising granulomas do not separate tuberculosis from sarcoidosis; sarcoidosis is a diagnosis of exclusion.
Never start high-dose steroid for presumed sarcoidosis without cover when miliary tuberculosis is still possible.
In secondary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, treating the trigger is the only intervention clearly linked to survival.
ground_truth.treatment_given: High-dose steroid for presumed sarcoidosis (curator's day 7); then dexamethasone and etoposide (HLH-2004, day 15); empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics and antifungals, intubation and vasopressors from day 18; rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol from day 25 with HLH chemotherapy withheld.

reports.impression: Diffuse bilateral miliary nodular pattern. Differential: disseminated granulomatous infection (mycobacterial or fungal), sarcoidosis, metastatic disease. CT chest recommended.
reports.report_text: Frontal chest radiograph. Innumerable small (1-3 mm) well-defined nodules distributed evenly through both lungs from apex to base. No consolidation, cavitation or pleural effusion. Hila and mediastinum not enlarged. Heart size normal.

reports.impression: Diffuse random (miliary) micronodules in both lungs, most in keeping with haematogenous dissemination: disseminated infection (mycobacterial or fungal) first; miliary sarcoidosis and metastases less likely without perilymphatic distribution or nodes. Splenomegaly.
reports.report_text: CT chest with contrast. Innumerable 1-3 mm nodules in a random distribution throughout both lungs, involving the subpleural lung and fissures, filling the entirety of both lungs. No cavitation, consolidation, tree-in-bud change or pleural effusion. No significant hilar or mediastinal lymph node enlargement. Visualised upper abdomen: the spleen is enlarged.

reports.impression: Moderate splenomegaly without focal lesions or lymphadenopathy.
reports.report_text: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Moderate splenomegaly (craniocaudal length 16 cm) with homogeneous enhancement and no focal lesion. Liver normal in size and attenuation. No abdominal or pelvic lymph node enlargement. Adrenal glands, kidneys and bowel normal. No ascites.

reports.impression: No pulmonary embolism. New diffuse bilateral airspace disease, progressive since admission: acute lung injury, infection or haemorrhage are the main considerations.
reports.report_text: CT pulmonary angiogram. No filling defect in the pulmonary arteries. New widespread bilateral airspace opacities with ground-glass change and dependent consolidation, superimposed on the known diffuse micronodules; progressive since the admission CT. Small bilateral pleural effusions. Endotracheal tube in a satisfactory position.

reports.impression: Normal airways. Lavage and transbronchial biopsies taken.
reports.report_text: Flexible bronchoscopy under sedation. Vocal cords normal. Trachea and bronchi to subsegmental level normal apart from mild mucosal erythema; no endobronchial lesion; scanty clear secretions. Bronchoalveolar lavage from the right middle lobe (150 mL instilled, 60 mL returned, sent for microbiology). Transbronchial biopsies from the right lower lobe; no significant bleeding.

reports.impression: Non-necrotising granulomatous inflammation. Special stains negative for organisms.
reports.report_text: Transbronchial lung biopsy (four fragments). Lung parenchyma containing several well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans-type multinucleate giant cells and a rim of lymphocytes. No caseous necrosis. Ziehl-Neelsen stain: no acid-fast bacilli seen. Grocott stain: no fungi seen. No vasculitis, dysplasia or malignancy.

reports.impression: Non-caseating granulomatous inflammation in the marrow; no lymphoma.
reports.report_text: Bone marrow trephine, 18 mm. Cellularity about 30%, reduced for age. Multiple small foci of non-caseating epithelioid granulomas with occasional giant cells. Trilineage haematopoiesis present with reduced granulopoiesis. No lymphoma or metastatic infiltrate. Ziehl-Neelsen stain: no acid-fast bacilli seen. Reticulin not increased.

reports.impression: Occasional haemophagocytic macrophages in a hypocellular marrow. No blasts or lymphoma cells.
reports.report_text: Bone marrow aspirate. Particulate but hypocellular. Occasional macrophages containing ingested red cells, platelets and neutrophil precursors. Myeloid to erythroid ratio 1.5:1; granulopoiesis reduced and left-shifted. Megakaryocytes present. No blasts; no abnormal lymphoid cells; plasma cells 3%.

reports.impression: No evidence of a lymphoproliferative disorder or increased blasts.
reports.report_text: Bone marrow flow cytometry. Lymphocytes 12% of events, polyclonal B cells (kappa:lambda 1.4) and T cells without aberrant antigen loss; CD4:CD8 ratio 1.1. Blasts 0.8%. No abnormal population.

reports.impression: No evidence of a circulating lymphoproliferative disorder.
reports.report_text: Peripheral blood flow cytometry. Lymphopenia; B, T and NK cells present in normal proportions; polyclonal B cells; no aberrant T-cell phenotype.

reports.impression: Granulomatous hepatitis, non-necrotising; special stains negative.
reports.report_text: Percutaneous liver biopsy, two cores. Several small non-necrotising epithelioid granulomas in portal tracts and lobules, with mild lobular inflammation and Kupffer cell hyperplasia. No caseous necrosis. Ziehl-Neelsen stain: no acid-fast bacilli seen. No steatosis, fibrosis or malignancy.

reports.impression: Normocytic anaemia with rouleaux and lymphopenia; morphology in keeping with chronic inflammation. Interpret the counts with the full blood count.
reports.report_text: Red cells normocytic and normochromic with mild anisocytosis and rouleaux. Lymphocytes reduced; those seen are small and mature. Neutrophils, where present, morphologically normal. Platelets normal in appearance. White cell and platelet numbers as in the accompanying full blood count. No blasts, parasites or red cell fragments.

reports.impression: Anaemia of chronic inflammation pattern; no features of a primary haematological disorder.
reports.report_text: Reviewed by a haematopathologist. Normocytic normochromic red cells with rouleaux; no spherocytes, fragments or inclusions. Lymphopenia; the lymphocytes are small and mature, without atypical or abnormal forms. Neutrophils, where present, without dysplasia. Platelets normal in appearance; their number as in the accompanying full blood count. No circulating haemophagocytes.

reports.impression: Negative for malaria parasites.
reports.report_text: Thick and thin films examined. No malaria parasites seen.

reports.impression: Splenomegaly without focal lesion.
reports.report_text: Ultrasound abdomen. Spleen enlarged at 15.5 cm with homogeneous echotexture and no focal lesion. Liver normal in size and echotexture. Gallbladder, bile ducts, pancreas and kidneys normal. No ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes seen.

reports.impression: Diffuse FDG-avid pulmonary micronodules with avid splenomegaly and marrow: an active systemic inflammatory or infectious process is likely; no nodal mass to suggest lymphoma.
reports.report_text: FDG PET-CT. Diffuse increased uptake through innumerable small nodules in both lungs. Diffusely increased uptake in an enlarged spleen and throughout the bone marrow. No FDG-avid lymph node mass, no focal bone lesion and no other focal abnormality.

reports.impression: Normal MRI brain.
reports.report_text: MRI brain with gadolinium. No focal parenchymal lesion, ring-enhancing lesion or abnormal meningeal enhancement. Ventricles normal in size. No hydrocephalus.

reports.impression: Sinus tachycardia; otherwise normal ECG.
reports.report_text: Sinus tachycardia 112/min. Normal axis. PR 150 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 432 ms. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

reports.impression: Normal echocardiogram; no vegetations or pericardial effusion.
reports.report_text: Transthoracic echocardiogram. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function, LVEF 62%, no regional wall motion abnormality. Normal right ventricle. Valves structurally normal; no vegetations. No pericardial effusion. Estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 30 mmHg.

reports.impression: Uncomplicated lumbar puncture with normal opening pressure.
reports.report_text: Lumbar puncture at L3-L4 in the left lateral position, atraumatic. Opening pressure 15 cmH2O. Clear, colourless CSF; samples sent for cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain and culture.

reports.impression: No deep vein thrombosis.
reports.report_text: Venous Doppler ultrasound of both legs. Common femoral, femoral and popliteal veins fully compressible with normal flow; calf veins patent.

reports.impression: Acute-phase pattern with polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia; no paraprotein.
reports.report_text: Serum protein electrophoresis. Albumin reduced. Alpha-1 and alpha-2 fractions increased. Diffuse polyclonal increase in the gamma region. No monoclonal band.
